# Version 5 Slide Montage — Markdown Visual Index

Purpose: provide a text-accessible index to the revised 21-slide visual sequence.

The visual story moves from intelligence to accountable physical action: the harness architecture, staged specialist work, evidence control, human approval, mission memory, MOXIE scale-up, portable skills and a bounded adoption path.

| Slide | Visual treatment | Primary visual purpose |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Mars settlement hero image | Establish the path from model intelligence to mission capability. |
| 2 | Mars surface image with capability tags | Show why knowledge alone does not execute physical work. |
| 3 | Four-layer harness stack | Show orchestration, context, tools, validation, approval and learning around swappable models. |
| 4 | Engineering control-room image | Ground durable skills in habitats, propulsion and operations. |
| 5 | Five-stage vertical sequence | Show Discover, Engineer, Verify, Deliver and Evolve. |
| 6 | Mars surface image with workflow tags | Introduce the scientific harness. |
| 7 | Four epistemic-status rows and control loop | Distinguish Observed, Derived, Assumed and Unknown from provenance. |
| 8 | Four-stage engineering blocks | Show requirements, trades, design and verification. |
| 9 | Six-row traceable handoff | Move status, uncertainty, requirement, test and approval together. |
| 10 | Mars operations image and authority roles | Show mandatory human approval for consequential action. |
| 11 | Five-row verification trace | Connect claims to sources, methods, results and gate state. |
| 12 | Four-stage mission-memory architecture | Preserve evidence, provenance, configuration, decisions, dissent and lessons. |
| 13 | Three-row local mission intelligence | Explain delay-tolerant operation. |
| 14 | Mars image and application map | Extend the pattern to rovers, habitats, ISRU, propulsion, power, medicine and construction. |
| 15 | ISRU digital-twin image and metric rows | Present verified MOXIE results without implying crew-scale readiness. |
| 16 | Mars engineering control room and requirements | Convert scale-up gaps into illustrative requirements and V&V. |
| 17 | Four-stage research-return loop | Return the solid-oxide stack-life design block to research. |
| 18 | Mars operations image and eight-skill map | Present platform-neutral portable skill contracts. |
| 19 | Five-stage adoption path | Pilot one consequential loop, validate it, then scale. |
| 20 | Mars settlement closing image | End on the harness as the path from intelligence to Mars. |

The original montage is a PNG overview. This Markdown representation preserves its slide order, visual logic and accessibility description.

## Version 1 visual principles

- SpaceX-like restraint and mission-control pacing.
- Approximately equal space for useful graphics and concise text.
- Infographics must show evidence, authority or work-product flow—not decorate the slide.
- Progressive diagrams should suggest motion while remaining understandable as static slides.
- Mars imagery is a forcing-function context for science, physical engineering and in-space operations.


---

## Version 5 visual narrative

Slides 1–5 establish the mission and architecture; 6–9 show the science, evidence, engineering, and handoff controls; 10–14 show the return loop, acceleration, verification, memory, and autonomy; 15–17 form the MOXIE/ISRU worked example; 18–21 show ecosystem, adoption, call to action, and closing. The rendered contact sheet was visually checked as a 21-slide deck.


---

## Updated slides 14–18

Slides 14–18 now form the case-study block: mission-scale MOXIE scenario; Hypatia research artifacts; engineering artifacts; project-planning artifacts; and the integrated science → engineering → plan/execute feedback loop. Slides 19–22 retain the portable-skills, adoption, call-to-action, and closing sequence.
